title: Confidence-weighted progressive rollout platform for model and runtime upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement: Our current rollout tools cover fixed-percentage canaries and simple health-based auto-rollback, but they lack contextual weighting for different traffic cohorts (internal, paid, free-tier, partner) and do not combine model-output quality signals with infra-level metrics when deciding ramp pace or rollback. This ticket builds a confidence-weighted progressive rollout system that uses cohort-specific risk profiles, statistical quality checks, and infrastructure health signals to drive % ramps, canary selection, feature-flag gating, and automated rollback. The goal is to reduce manual intervention for routine upgrades while keeping blast radius controlled for both runtime and model changes.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Rollout controller service enhancements
   - Implement cohort weighting: allow rollouts to specify multiple cohorts with independent ramp curves and weights (e.g., internal: 5% -> 20%, paid: 1% -> 15%, free: 0.1% -> 5%).
   - Confidence metric: compute a single composite confidence score per cohort by combining (a) infra metrics (p95 latency, error-rate), (b) model quality deltas (eval prompt-set pass-rate, semantic similarity drift), (c) business signals (conversion / engagement proxies).
   - Adaptive ramping policy: dynamic step changes based on confidence bands (green/yellow/red) with configurable step sizes and cooldown windows.

2) Gate definitions and automated rollback
   - Statistical tests: integrate A/B statistical significance checks (bootstrap CIs for token-level latency and model-quality metrics) to detect regressions early.
   - Multi-signal rollback policy: allow rules that combine signals (e.g., if p99 latency +10% AND model perplexity worsens >5% OR error-rate increase >0.5%) trigger rollback.
   - Safe fallback mechanism: automatically divert failing cohorts to a pinned LTS model or a lighter quantized variant while investigation proceeds.

3) Feature flag + API changes
   - Expose new rollout API fields in Redwood API and Console: cohorts[], weight_profiles[], confidence_thresholds, rollback_actions.
   - Backwards compatibility: if new fields omitted, controller behaves like existing percent-ramp canary.

4) Observability and runbooks
   - Console dashboard tile: per-cohort confidence score, ramp history, active gates, and predicted next step.
   - Runbook and alert playbooks for escalations and postmortems.

Acceptance criteria:
- Can define a rollout with at least 3 cohorts and independent ramps via Console and API.
- Automated ramp decisions respect configured confidence thresholds and enter cooldowns on anomalous signals.
- Rollback actions can route traffic to an LTS or fallback model automatically and generate an incident note with relevant metrics.
- E2E tests and simulation harness that can replay production traffic and inject anomalies to validate rollback triggers.

Design decisions / tradeoffs:
- Composite confidence score trades sensitivity for noise suppression: by default we apply weighted smoothing to avoid flip-flopping on short spikes. We will expose smoothing window and sensitivity knobs for power users.
- We prioritize safety over fast rollouts: default configs will be conservative for public customers, with more aggressive defaults for internal/QA cohorts.
- Statistical tests will initially run on aggregated cohort windows (5–15m) to balance timeliness vs false positives; we may shorten windows for internal cohorts later.

Integration points and dependencies:
- Console: UI components to edit cohorts and visualize confidence timeline. (frontend PR required)
- Metrics pipeline: new model-quality metrics ingestion (eval-runner -> metrics-db) to be available to controller.
- Routing layer: capability to pin traffic to specific model versions / fallbacks.

Migration and versioning plan:
- New rollout API will be opt-in for existing customers. We will provide a migration guide demonstrating how to express equivalent behavior in the new model.
- LTS channel awareness: when a rollout references an upgrade that is not LTS, customers can configure a fallback LTS version to be used automatically if confidence < threshold.

Security and compliance:
- No customer PII is used in confidence score calculations; only aggregated metrics and non-identifying engagement signals. KMS access required for retrieving rollout secrets and feature-flag keys.

Testing and staging plan:
- Simulation harness in staging that replays sampled production traffic across cohorts and injects latency/errors and model-quality perturbations.
- Unit tests for statistical modules, integration tests for rollback flows, and chaos-tests that validate safe fallback under network partitions.

Rollout plan for this feature:
- Week 1: implement core controller and scheduler; API schema and backend.
- Week 2: metrics hooks and confidence calculation; basic UI mockups.
- Week 3: integrate rollout into Console; implement fallback routing and automatic rollback actions.
- Week 4: E2E tests, simulation runs, and a canary with internal-only traffic.

Longer-term considerations:
- Add ML-driven tuning of weights for confidence score per-customer based on historical rollback outcomes.
- Support for cross-region staggered ramps and differential region risk tolerances.

Estimated effort: 8 points.
